section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the statistical analyses used to evaluate the Polish BAS-2, including a two-stage factor analytic approach with separate analyses for a first and second subsample, and testing measurement invariance across men and women. It reports use of principal-axis factor analysis and CFA (AMOS v.22), fit indices (CFI, RMSEA, SRMR, -2 statistics), Cronbach's alpha for internal consistency, independent-samples t-test to compare genders, and Pearson correlations with BMI and other constructs for convergent validity. The text explicitly mentions analyses on a first subsample and a second subsample but does not label separate studies.
section_summary.evidence_source: A two-stage factor analytic approach was adopted to examine the factor structure of the BAS-2. Data from the first subsample was analysed using a principal-axis factor analysis (without rotation) for women and men separately, whereas data from the second subsample was analysed by means of CFA using AMOS v.22 (Arbuckle, 2005). Cronbach's ˛ was used to investigate the internal consistency of Polish BAS-2 scores. Pearson correlation coefficients between body appreciation and self-esteem, body-related emotions, positive affect, positive orientation, and BMI were calculated to establish the convergent validity of the scale.
